tfn.s: Nine chefs and food writers were asked about their own children.
tfn.why: The text says: “The Guardian's Mina Holland asked nine chefs and food writers what their own children eat at home, and the honesty of the answers is the most striking thing about them.”

tfn.s: All of the cooks refuse to make a separate meal for a child.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: “Anna Jones admits she cannot bring herself to send a child to bed hungry, so she does make alternatives, while Mitchell and Rosie Birkett mostly do not.”

tfn.s: Helen Goh tells her sons exactly what is in the food.
tfn.why: The text says: “Helen Goh cooks onions, carrots and celery into a base and grates courgette until it melts away, but she tells her sons exactly what is in it.”

tfn.s: The chefs' children are healthier than average.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text reports what the children eat but makes no comparison with anybody else.
